### The block, and why it mattered (round 1 verdict: BLOCK)
Chris did not block on process. He found my photosensitivity probe **measuring the wrong pixel**.

`coreLuma()` sampled a fixed 40x40 window at the CSS gradient's declared centre (22%/24%) — where
the bolt's ALPHA peaks — and reported luminance delta **0.0199**. His independent full-viewport
scan found the true worst case is **0.073 at x=13.2%**: ~4x higher, and somewhere else.

    delta(x,y) = alpha(x,y) x (flash_colour - background(x,y))

The backdrop is a PHOTOGRAPH, so background luminance varies spatially. Peak visible CONTRAST sits
where alpha is still strong AND the cloud beneath is dark — not where alpha peaks. I assumed they
coincided because the CSS names one point. Same measure-a-proxy error as the original flash-count
bug, recurring INSIDE the probe written to close that gap — spatial this time instead of temporal.
**Choosing where to sample is itself a claim that needs verifying.**

### The fix (415e9306a, one file: storm-safety-probe.js)
`worstLumaDelta()` screenshots at alpha=0 and at the page-read peak, pauses every `.env-plane` so
the bolt is the ONLY variable, converts to WCAG relative luminance, block-averages 10x10, and
scans EVERY block for the maximum.

    at 13.2% / 23.3%:  rest 0.0994 -> peak 0.1726  (delta 0.0732)
    margin to the WCAG 0.10 general-flash threshold: 27%

Chris got 0.0729 at the same coords. Two independently written scans agree to 0.0003.
**Conclusion survives** — under 0.10 means not a flash under 2.3.1 at all, with honest 27% margin
rather than the huge margin I claimed. Ships with the measured number, not the flattering one.

Also corrected: I quoted the scoping probe as 15/15; it prints **18/18**. Stale, my error, his catch.
